output.sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(o.net_revenue), 2) AS avg_order_value, COUNT(*) AS revenue_orders FROM marts.fct_orders o WHERE o.is_revenue AND o.order_date >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND o.order_date < DATE '2026-01-01';
output.explanation: The query averages net_revenue across 2025 orders and rounds the result to 2 decimals. It only counts orders where is_revenue is true, so cancelled orders and other non-revenue orders don't affect the average. It uses order_date to place orders in 2025, and the second column shows how many orders went into the average. Net revenue is the amount after discounts, not counting shipping fees.
